text:
Tony DeAngelo has settled into the middle of the Islanders' blue line, and the minutes are climbing: 18:06 a night overall, 19:29 over his last ten. The scoring hasn't followed yet, with 8 points in 24 games after 35 in 76 last season. Our numbers point to bad luck there. New York has scored 5.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which costs a puck-moving defenseman assists.

The playmaking is real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.3 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 91st percentile among defensemen, and carrying the puck in on 40% of his entries. The flaw is the same one that has followed him around the league: only 29% of his exits kept possession, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.25 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, bottom 1% of defensemen. This year the 5-on-5 chances are split evenly with him out there, which is an improvement worth watching. Our numbers project about 33 points.
headline: DeAngelo's points should come; his own end is the question
